air.en: dictionary, area, paragraph, very, secondary, necessary

questions.why: Where CMUdict has the short i before r (here, near, year), you write ī: 14 times, against 2 times i (experiences ikspirīxnsiz, experiencing ikspirīxnsīngg, though experience is ekspīriins). As a rule it’s worth 8 more words now, and it would cover every new word like it.

options.why: make it a rule, and fix experiences and experiencing

questions.ask: yü for the weak u after y: always?
questions.why: In -ular, -ulous, -uable and -ure, CMUdict has a weak vowel after y (kyxlr). You always write yü there: prtikyülr, vōkæbyülerī, mitikyülxslī, vælyüibl, kyürētid. 4 for 4 where it’s the only difference.

You write 4 in dictionary (dikšin4ī), area (4īx), barrier (b4īr), paragraph (p4xgræf), but e or æ in very (verī ×14), cherries (cerīz), error (err), american (xmerikin), and -erī in secondary, necessary, commentary. I can’t find one rule that fits all of these. Is there one, or is it word by word?

options.why: keep each as you wrote it; new words get CMUdict’s e/æ
dictionary, secondary, necessary, commentary all 4ī; very and error stay

questions.ask: ex- at the start: ik or ek?
questions.why: Mostly ik/ig: igzæktlī, igzämpxl, igzist, ikstenšin, ikspirīxnsiz. But eks in except (eksept), explain (eksplēn) and expensive (ekspensiv), and experience is ekspīriins. Is there a pattern, or are the eks ones slips?

options.why: it depends on how I say the word; keep them

questions.why: The converter drops the vowel after b (table tēbl, assembled xsembld), but you wrote capable kēpxbxl, global glōbxl and symbol simbxl ×2. Which is it?

options.why: keep the vowel: tēbxl, kēpxbxl, simbxl

questions.ask: ng then g inside a word?
questions.why: You write the g in finger (fīnggr) and longer (lánggr), and in every -ing (thīngg), but not in English (īngliš) or languages (lēngwijiz). Is English the exception, or does the g depend on the word?

options.text: English and languages are the exceptions

questions.ask: x or i: does the grader need to care?
questions.why: The biggest pile left: 135 words differ from you only in the unstressed vowel, x or i. A rule now gets you i before a final d, z, n, t or s, but the rest look like free choice. If x and i are the same to you in an unstressed syllable, the grader could count either as right. If they’re different sounds to you, I keep looking for rules.

options.text: They’re the same to me there
